description: A failure that may succeed later: `429` rate limit, `500` server error, `503` or `529` overloaded, `504` timeout. A `400` such as `context_length` fails the same way every time.
The provider's hint (a header on `429` and `503`) for how long to wait. It overrides your computed backoff.
A random delay between zero and the capped exponential backoff, so clients that failed together do not retry together.
Send every request to a cheap model first and escalate to a stronger one only when a mechanical check rejects the answer.
The share of requests the cheap tier could not handle. When it climbs, the cascade stops saving money.
A second provider or self-hosted model used after the primary exhausts its retries on availability errors.
The set of components that fail together. A fallback must sit in a different one: another provider or region, not another model behind the same outage.
A dated snapshot id instead of an alias such as `-latest`, so behavior changes only when you deploy a change.
